title: Laki extension (widget.json)
description: A Laki extension: what it fetches, how often, where it shows and what it draws (ui). https://github.com/igorkasyanchuk/laki/blob/main/docs/extensions.md

description.description: A line about it, in Settings

size.description: Cells across (1-3) and down (½, 1-4) in the sidebar; across in a bar

view.description: Its full view’s size: s, m (the default) or l

anyOf.description: side (the sidebar), top or status (a bar, a line high), rail or foot (a button), desk (the Desk)

items.description: side (the sidebar), top or status (a bar, a line high), rail or foot (a button), desk (the Desk)

place.description: Where it shows at first (the user’s choice wins): one place or several

fetch.description: A shell command in its folder; what it prints (JSON) is its data. $WIDGET_<NAME> per setting, $LAKI_WIDGET_CONFIG, $LAKI_REFRESH_REASON

script.description: Or a JS file of its folder: its default export gets { config, last } and returns the data

additionalProperties.description: A setting: its default (text; a number, true/false or a list make that kind), or a spec

type.description: text, number, bool (a switch), choice (one of choices) or list (chips)

config.description: Its settings, by name (a letter or _, then letters, digits, _)

actions.description: Commands its buttons run by name, with $WIDGET_ARG; what one prints as JSON may say { "toast" } or { "modal" }

icon.description: As a button: an icon of Laki’s by name, or an emoji

label.description: As a button: its words, a template over its data

badge.description: As a button: a short count, a template ("{{#if n}}{{n}}{{/if}}")

click.description: One of its actions, run on a click on its button

sample.description: Made-up data in the shape its fetch prints, for its preview before it runs (needed with a fetch)

sampleConfig.description: Settings to show the sample with

ui.description: What it draws with the UI kit (Settings › Extensions › UI kit, laki widget kit): one element, or { "preview", "full" }
What it draws with the UI kit: one element (the preview and the full view), or { "preview", "full" }
